0.3Diagram notation

Sequence diagrams

  • Solid arrow: request, command or event sent.
  • Dashed arrow: result, acknowledgement or returned state.
  • Band with accent edge: operator (alt, else, opt, loop, par, guard) and its condition in brackets; band with dark edge: named phase of the flow.
  • PDF figures number steps 01, 02 …; detail figures number steps 1, 2, ….

State machines and flows

  • Filled dot: initial state. Tinted box: target or terminal state of interest.
  • Transition label: triggering event, then the guard in brackets where stated.
  • Dashed connector: feedback, return or recovery path.
  • Diamond: decision; every outcome is labelled.

0.5Scope and document structure

This specification defines the proposed product, service and system design of a regional autonomous mobility service with integrated reservation, dispatch, energy coordination and remote operation. It covers the customer touchpoints and their measurement (Part 1), the common platform, its containers, interfaces, remote operation and capacity rules (Part 2), and their requirements, interfaces and open decisions (Appendices C–E). Vehicle-internal automated driving functions are outside its scope; the ADS retains the dynamic driving task and fallback (P14).

Part 1 · Product management supplement

Mobility service planning / Product management supplementP01 / 30

Customer touchpoints and mobility service value

A proposed service model connects consented intent to reachable supply, additional activity and feasible travel choices.

01Product outcome & scope

Product hypothesis

Customer intent and shared transport capacity can improve service outcomes through five testable mechanisms.

Consented signalsIntended arrival, booking lead time, free-time interval and optional preferences. Purpose, expiry and withdrawal remain explicit.

Resident / visitor

Share plans, free time and preferences with consent. Retain control of timing, price and accessibility needs.

Mobility operator

Position reachable vehicles, protect committed trips and own exceptions within finite operating capacity.

Service provider

Return activity slots, prices and service capacity. Confirm reservations and observed use.

City partner

Set ODD, access and coverage conditions. Review outcomes for underserved places and users.

MaaS product layer

C01 identity / API → C02 booking & consent → C03 feasibility / reservation → C04 dispatch & status → C06 support / cases → C07 usage / settlement  |  C05 energy capability constrains feasible supply

Decision inputsIntent, reachable supply, provider slots, hub / energy limits and accepted terms

End-to-end service loop
  1. 01Intent
  2. 02Feasible offer
  3. 03Confirmed plan
  4. 04Trip + support
  5. 05Verified outcome

Five value mechanisms / Information and shared capacity

01 Advance positioning

  • InputReceived plan + lead time.
  • ActionPosition reachable supply before pickup.
  • TestWait, empty km and unmet demand.
  • LimitCancellation, forecast error and energy.

02 Additional demand

  • InputFree time + preference + spare capacity.
  • ActionOffer a feasible activity and trip.
  • TestAdditional use and net contribution.
  • LimitSubstitution and induced congestion.

03 Demand smoothing

  • InputFlexible window + alternative total price.
  • ActionMove an accepted trip in time.
  • TestPeak load and missed pickups.
  • LimitRefusal and discount cost.
04 Shared rides / 05 Passenger–freight sharing

Match compatible passenger journeys within seat, access and detour limits. Test passenger output, discounts and net contribution. 05: Insert eligible cargo within payload, space and handling limits. Include freight revenue, added dwell and displaced passenger trips. Detailed operating conditions: P29–P30.

SERVICE CONTRACT C02 keeps each passenger / shipment intent. C03 checks route and segment capacity. C04 records the shared mission. C06 owns passenger recovery and cargo exceptions. C07 reconciles revenue and shared costs. C05 constrains energy.
VALUE TEST Protect consent and accepted service limits. Report additional demand, shifted demand and shared-route efficiency separately. Include rejection, cancellation, handling and recovery. Capacity / continuity: P25–P28. Sharing rules: P29–P30.

Mobility service planning / Product management supplementP02 / 30

End-to-end journey across user, operation and platform

Passenger bookings, activity reservations and shipments retain distinct identities through shared routes, revised offers and verified outcomes.

02Service blueprint

STAGE EVIDENCE Plan: consent + receipt time   Request: eligible offer + capacity   Confirm: accepted terms + committed holds   Travel: observed pickup + owned exception   Complete: trip / activity actuals + cost

Exception loop

A revised plan releases obsolete holds only after reconciliation. Cancellation or capacity loss updates positioning, ETA and the recovery owner.

Traceability contract
intentId + passenger / shipmentId + bookingRev + routeRev + missionId

Record offers, accepted terms, original / revised times, route stops and segment occupancy. Link every passenger and shipment to observed boarding, alighting or delivery. Preserve source / receipt time, consent and custody evidence. Shared mission costs remain unique.

Acceptance invariants

Positioning uses information already received. Commit all required holds before confirmation. Check seats, accessible space, payload and cargo volume on every segment. Recompute existing passenger limits after insertion. Time shifts preserve request identity. Suggestions need acceptance. Unknown effects require reconciliation. Completion uses passenger / cargo evidence separately. Each exception retains an owner and deadline.

← P01Customer touchpoints and mobility service valueP03 →MVP boundary and product prioritization

Mobility service planning / Product management supplementP03 / 30

MVP boundary and product prioritization

A complete service slice provides the baseline. Five controlled mechanisms test information value and shared-capacity economics.

03MVP & prioritization

Priority rule

Rank by measured service benefit, net contribution, feasibility and learning value.

Common fleet / hubs / demand conditions support comparison. Capacity and service guardrails remain binding.

Dependency orderReliable request / outcome records precede effect measurement. Finite capacity and recovery precede offer expansion.

Pilot MVP

One selected service slice

  1. 01Capture intent, needs, consent and idempotent request
  2. 02Return feasible options, binding reasons and expiry
  3. 03Commit booking + resource bundle with revision checks
  4. 04Track state, freshness, support case and recovery owner
  5. 05Reconcile actual trip, service use and passenger outcome

Exit only when normal + recovery paths pass acceptance; operator can resolve exceptions; event and cost records reconcile.
Required evidence: valid, rejected, cancelled and recovered journeys. Reconcile every request to one final disposition and every cost to one owner.

Iterate

Five controlled mechanisms

  1. 01Use received plans for feasible advance positioning
  2. 02Offer activities within spare time and capacity
  3. 03Shift accepted trips with clear timing and price
  4. 04Pool compatible riders within each detour limit
  5. 05Insert eligible cargo within payload and time limits

Advance when gains survive service guardrails, realistic acceptance, full costs and supply stress.
Retain independent controls for all five effects. Test late signals, substitution, peak overload, no-shows, cargo dwell and failed handovers.

Extend platform

Repeatable operating model

  1. 01Versioned adapters and purpose-limited consent
  2. 02Energy, hub throughput and staffing in feasibility
  3. 03Guarded support and owned passenger recovery
  4. 04Calibrate by zone, time and user segment
  5. 05Reusable configuration, evidence and rollback

Expand after second-site tests preserve service quality and net contribution with local demand, capacity and operating costs. Replication tests: different OD pattern, provider capacity, support load and energy limits. Retain tenant isolation and configuration / policy versions.

MVP control

MVP entry criteria: selected geography / ODD / channel / segment; named service and incident owners; provider, fleet and site capacity confirmed; legal, privacy, accessibility and partner constraints reviewed; C01–C07 data and authority boundaries agreed. Pilot exit: normal + cancellation + disruption / recovery traces pass; queue and support coverage are staffed; KPI baseline, missing-data behavior and cost ledger reconcile; rollback and customer communication are rehearsed. Optional C05 optimization, remote assistance and I09 roadside sensing stay out until separately gated.

G2 constraint register: ODD = approved operating conditions (road, speed, weather, time, etc.). DDT = real-time operational / tactical functions needed to operate in traffic (including OEDR); record which actor performs them. Define DDT fallback separately by actor, trigger, response and intervention boundary. Also record operating limits (hours / staffing / recovery), infrastructure (node power / energy / footprint) and business limits (fare / demand / transit overlap). For each, record variable, unit / value or TBD, source URL, owner, affected KPI and PL line. Set thresholds only after evidence and ownership are confirmed. Source: SAE J3016_202609, doi:10.4271/J3016_202609.

D03.1Decision logicMVP → iterate → extend as evidence gates

Each column advances only when its exit condition holds. Gates are evidence checkpoints, not calendar phases: a failed condition returns to the earliest gate whose assumption is invalidated, and scope stays held until the named owner closes the gap.

ExpandSecond-site tests preserve service quality and net contribution with local demand, capacity and operating costs.Different OD pattern, provider capacity, support load and energy limits; tenant isolation and configuration / policy versions.G5 / Repeat

Usability tasks to test

Test optional data access, original choice, revised timing and total cost. Measure success, decision time, comprehension, opt-out and acceptance by accessibility need. Include refusal, stale capacity, cancellation after positioning and lost ACK.
Users must identify the committed plan, decline while retaining the original option and reach help. Operators must explain infeasibility, protect commitments and recover without duplicates. Record critical errors and failed recovery separately.

Prototype evidence: decision time, price / timing comprehension, recovery completion and reasons for refusal. No forced consent or automatic schedule change.

State model 
DRAFT → QUOTED (expiresAt) → PENDING (hold) → CONFIRMED (commit) → IN_SERVICE → COMPLETED (actuals + passenger outcome) / CANCELLED (reason + release). Timeout / lost acknowledgement → UNKNOWN → query and reconcile; never duplicate a side effect. Revision conflict → refresh terms; stale evidence → block offer or action with reason.

04 / 05 Shared-capacity measures

Passenger output, freight delivery and net contribution

Passenger journeys / vehicle-hour; seat-km utilization; detour; freight delivery / lateness; cargo dwell; displaced passenger trips. Detail: P29–P30.

Measurement contract

Service gates apply to each passenger and shipment. Separate booking counts, people, deliveries and vehicle missions. Targets require baseline evidence.

ATTRIBUTION: separate additional demand, time shifts, substitution, pooled passengers and delivered shipments. A shared route has several intents but one vehicle mission. Count route distance and common costs once. Effects 01–03 use matched inputs. Compare 04 / 05 in four conditions, then test interactions.
SERVICE: retain unserved passenger and cargo requests. Check pickup / arrival promises, detour, seats, payload, volume, hub queues and recovery. Report passenger and freight fulfillment separately. Confirm observed use and custody outcomes.
FINANCE: net passenger fares already reflect sharing discounts and displaced trips. Add recognized freight revenue, then deduct route, handling, energy, support, cleaning, recovery, returns and app costs once. Show total contribution alongside unit measures. Keep CAPEX and project cash flow distinct.

Controlled experiments and evidence workflow

Simulation tests five mechanisms under stated assumptions. Field trials measure actual acceptance, shared-route performance and handling time.

06Discovery & validation

Evidence loopObserve demand and choices / calibrate assumptions / repeat comparisons / approve the next bounded test

D06.1SequenceEvidence workflow from observation to a recorded decision

One pass of the evidence loop: field observations are framed into a scenario, compared in paired simulation runs, checked in a bounded pilot and closed by the accountable owner with a documented continue / revise / stop decision.

Experiment design / Attribution and interaction

  1. Baseline
    • All effects off
    • Same fleet / hubs
    • Same demand and faults
    • Fixed accounting basis
    • Demand / outage trace fixed
    • Same cost boundary
  2. Isolated effects
    • Effects 01–03 alone
    • Pooling only
    • Cargo only
    • Paired outcome tests
    • Fixed shared inputs
    • Separate effect controls
  3. Combined effects
    • Pooling + cargo
    • Four conditions
    • 01–03 held fixed
    • Then all five effects
    • Capacity interaction
    • Cost counted once
  4. Field check
    • Sharing acceptance
    • Actual detour / wait
    • Cargo dwell / delivery
    • Net service and cost
    • Assignment / spillover
    • Stop / rollback rules
Stress tests

Sweep lead time, forecast error, acceptance, substitution and discounts. Vary route overlap, party size, allowed detour, cargo mass / volume, handling time and delivery windows. Test peak demand, hub loss, no-shows, absent recipients and vehicle recovery. Preserve passenger / shipment identity. Reject future-information leakage. Gains fail when realistic costs erase contribution or any accepted service limit breaks.

Proposed tests only. Simulation outputs do not establish field impact or guarantee service-level attainment.

Reproducible evidence record

Record engine / scenario version, input units / sources, demand trace, information receipt times, initial fleet / hub state, seed and effect switches. Retain offer / intent linkage, acceptance, original / revised time, trip / activity actuals, rejected demand and ledger entries. Report paired differences and uncertainty across repeated runs.
Field design: predefine assignment unit, observation window and thresholds. Shared vehicles create spillover across users and zones. Check non-participation, displacement and rebound demand. Keep simulated acceptance distinct from measured behavior.
Decision packet: input provenance, reproducible run, outcome distribution, guardrail failures, sensitivity, accountable owner and a documented continue / revise / stop decision. Unsupported effects stay unvalidated.

D06.2Decision logicWhen a measured gain fails or stays unvalidated

Checks applied to a paired comparison before it can enter the decision packet. A run that leaks future information or loses passenger / shipment identity is rejected; a gain that breaks a service limit or is erased by realistic costs fails.

Source: P06 stress tests; P06 reproducible evidence record; P06 experiment design

Mobility service planning / Product management supplementP07 / 30

Roadmap from discovery to repeatable deployment

Each gate adds evidence for customer response, operating feasibility and net value before the service expands.

07Release & scale gates

  1. G1 / DISCOVER

    Select users, zones and time windows. Observe lead time, unmet demand, activity alternatives and willingness to shift. Establish traceable service and cost baselines. Record sampling gaps and consent boundaries.

    • EvidenceJourney / demand map, request denominators, alternatives and constraints.
    • CheckMissing demand and selection bias.
    • OwnerPM + Operations.
    GO / HOLD / REVISE
  2. G2 / DEFINE

    Define five mechanisms and separate controls. Prototype sharing, detour, price and cargo terms. Set passenger and freight gates, cost boundaries and comparison design. Agree consent, capacity and custody ownership before evaluation.

    • EvidenceCausal model, offer tests, KPI dictionary and comparison design.
    • CheckConsent, cost boundary and failure criteria.
    • OwnerPM + Design + Finance.
    GO / HOLD / REVISE
  3. G3 / PILOT READY

    Pass C01–C07 normal and fault paths. Verify seat / payload limits per segment, route revisions, no duplicate intents and auditable costs. Staff passenger recovery and cargo handling. Rehearse no-show, failed delivery and rollback.

    • EvidenceAcceptance traces, finite capacity, ledger and staffed recovery.
    • CheckFault injection and rollback rehearsal.
    • OwnerEngineering + Operations.
    GO / HOLD / REVISE
↓
  1. G4 / LEARN

    Compare individual and combined effects with matched inputs. Measure sharing acceptance, detour and handling time. Retain displaced passenger trips and failed deliveries. Check service gates and net contribution under realistic conditions.

    • EvidenceEffect range, adverse outcomes, full costs and counter-evidence.
    • CheckNet gain survives realistic response.
    • OwnerPM + Operations + Finance.
    GO / HOLD / REVISE
  2. ← G5 / REPEAT

    Repeat at a second site with local demand, provider capacity and costs. Confirm gains survive weak acceptance and supply loss. Package configuration, training, monitoring and recovery. Approve expansion within a verified operating envelope.

    • EvidenceSecond-site results, support cost, sensitivity and partner acceptance.
    • CheckLocal limits preserve service and value.
    • OwnerRollout lead + site owner.
    GO / HOLD / REVISE
  3. HOLD / REPLAN RULES

    Schedule alone never passes a gate. HOLD for unresolved safety / privacy / legal risk, unknown execution, missing evidence, unstaffed support, partner unreadiness, unreliable data or unreconciled cost.

    REVISE with named owner, required evidence, deadline and temporary scope restriction. Return to an earlier gate when new evidence changes the user problem or service boundary. Record rollback trigger and resume authority.

Gate transition ruleGates are evidence checkpoints, not fixed calendar phases. A failed condition returns to the earliest gate whose assumption is invalidated; scope stays held until the named owner closes the evidence gap and the decision is recorded.

Product decision ownership

PM owns user outcomes, scope and KPI decisions. Design owns comprehension and accessibility. Engineering owns contracts, trace quality and release. Operations / partners own service capacity and recovery. Finance verifies revenue scope, cost allocation and investment assumptions. Every HOLD has a named closure owner.

Decision basis

Service feasibility and customer choice remain binding even when aggregate contribution improves.

Technical evidence in the following system design

Reservation and service contracts: slides 8–11 • Remote operation and roadside interfaces: slides 13–23 • Fault injection and release dependencies: slide 24

Capacity, replenishment, recovery and verification: P25–P28. Shared rides and passenger–freight rules: P29–P30. All tests remain proposed.

GO / HOLD record

Decision + date • user segment / site • baseline and observed KPI • acceptance trace • unresolved safety / legal / operational risk • scope restriction • accountable owner • next review trigger. GO requires named service owner, trained operation, support coverage, data quality and rollback path. Finance record: CAPEX and OPEX by node and project; node and project payback; IRR; sensitivity range; Variable / Value / Source URL / formula-use link for every assumption.

1.2Runtime deployment, isolation and recovery

  1. RESTORERestore domain state, consent, outboxes and command history.
  2. RECONCILERebuild projections and verify external effects by original IDs.
  3. ENABLE DISPATCHFence the writer, confirm freshness and operator-approved readiness.

Connector failure may leave local intake available; confirmation still requires all mandatory dependencies. Stale vehicle/site state blocks affected capacity. Replay must use separate projections and idempotent effect handlers.

G2 decisions: hosting zones, failover mechanism, protocols, RPO/RTO, latency and freshness budgets. The primary service integrates booking, dispatch and energy. Equipment/JV/eVTOL options attach through capability interfaces.

Departure guard: all required tasks finish before departure; precedence permits only approved overlap. Electrical branch:

E_dep = E_arr + Σ(η_ch P_AC Δt_h) − E_aux
with E_trip + E_reserve ≤ E_dep ≤ E_usable,max
kW × hours = kWh

2.3Selected reservation transitions and replacement constraints

Replacement holds new capacity before retiring old. Swap applies only to unstarted allocations. Started/unknown missions retain occupancy until physical clearance. PENDING does not expire on quote TTL. Cancellation uses P11; shared seats enforce summed capacity per segment.

Shared rides and cargo require segment capacity, route revision and distinct booking outcomes (P29–P30). Count the vehicle cycle once, including empty travel, boarding, cargo dwell, turnaround and energy. Reserve loading bays, staff and hub capacity separately (P25–P26).

D09.2SequenceAmend by atomic replacement: hold new before retiring old

Amending a CONFIRMED booking keeps the old allocation while the new bundle is held and committed. The swap applies only to unstarted allocations; old physical capacity is released only after vehicle / EMS clearance.

7.2Operational roles and failure containment

Remote assistance and remote driving

RA supplies contextual advice that the ADS can reject after re-evaluating the scene and ODD. Real-time remote DDT is outside this baseline. Adding remote driving requires a distinct operating envelope, control arbitration, communications safety analysis and operator / approval evidence.

Operational and legal responsibility

Map system roles to the permitted operation, designated supervisor and field-response organisation. Passenger support cannot override door interlocks or authorise motion. Vehicle-specific link-loss and fallback behaviour remains local and does not depend on a remote reply.

  1. Active authority
    • Durable cases / command journal
    • Replicated evidence + backlog
    • Vehicle fence ACK gates new actions
  2. Standby promotion
    • Acquire higher authority epoch
    • Require vehicle fence ACK (P20)
    • Reconcile prior effects before action
  3. Degraded service
    • Hold affected assignments
    • Preserve priority safety traffic
    • Escalate without hiding uncertainty

Acceptance: independently partition telemetry, media, primary centre and workstation. Old-epoch requests reject after the vehicle installs its fence. Test durable deduplication and unknown outcomes. Reconnect and case closure require the release predicate on P18 before availability can change.

D14.2SequenceAuthority hand-over: standby promotion with vehicle fence ACK

Expands the Active authority → Standby promotion → Degraded service flow of §7.2. The new centre acquires a higher authority epoch, but gains action rights per vehicle only after that vehicle durably installs the fence; unreachable vehicles stay in degraded service with capacity held.

D14.3State machineCentre authority per vehicle: active, standby, degraded

Centre ownership and vehicle action rights are separate. New cloud ownership does not instantly revoke an unreachable vehicle's old authority, so the per-vehicle state stays in degraded service until a fence ACK arrives.

Reconnect alone does not restore availability: reconnect and case closure require the release predicate on P18. No automatic re-entry on reconnect.

9.2Fault branches and planned verification

LINK / EDGE LOSS

Heartbeat expiry → coverage UNKNOWN; retain source time. No stale frame displayed as current. Reconnect uses new epoch, resync + health checks; replay is historical only. Test disconnect, reboot, reordering, duplicate delivery.

CONFLICT / OVERLOAD

Keep both source claims; no silent override of ADS state. Overload reports queue age and dropped observations. Test occlusion, weather, false association and saturation. Measure quality, end-to-end age and operator workload.

Autonomous mobility service / System planning — Initial conceptP17 / 30

Telemetry coverage and alarm decision logic

RM-03 / RM-04. Capability-specific signals feed versioned detection and triage. Alarm priorities are operational response classes, not ASIL classifications. Every action uses current, valid evidence.

10.1Signal families, decision context and missing-data behaviour

ADS / ODD

  • adsMode, engagementState, oddVerdict/reason, oddProfileRev
  • Route / geofence / weather / illumination constraints as supported.

ODD or mode inconsistency opens a case. Cloud context never widens ODD.

Motion / localisation

  • pose + coordinateFrame, speed, heading, localisationHealth
  • Covariance and integrity bounds remain distinct supplier quantities.

Detect unexpected stop / deviation. Uncertain pose cannot prove location.

Perception / planning

  • sensorHealth, occlusionFlags, plannerStatus, blockageReason
  • assistanceRequest + sceneRev + mapRev + frame capture time

Review ambiguity in context. Generic “AI confidence” cannot permit motion.

Chassis / fallback

  • brake / steering / propulsion health, emergencyStopStatus
  • fallbackReason, mrmState, mrcAchieved, standstill / secureState

Separate manoeuvre progress from achieved MRC. Failed fallback escalates.

Passenger / mission

  • missionId/rev, pickup/drop-off state, door/ramp/restraint status
  • SOS, occupancy quality, accessibility and handover exceptions

Local interlocks prevail. Unknown occupancy requires supported confirmation.

Energy / link

  • SOC, usableEnergy, HV/thermal fault, departure reserve margin
  • heartbeat, RTT, loss, jitter, mediaAge, seqGap, clockQuality

Energy shortage revises feasibility. Link loss marks remote state UNKNOWN.

10.2Evidence validation, alarm lifecycle and response classes

  1. Validate / detect
    • Identity, schema, unit, epoch/seq
    • Age / source quality / clock bound
    • Predicate + persistence + hysteresis
  2. Correlate / assign
    • Vehicle / cause / incident window
    • Severity + exposure + dueAt
    • Qualified seat + ACK + lease
  3. Act / verify / clear
    • Guard action and observe outcome
    • Stable clear condition + release
    • Reopen on contradictory evidence
P0Collision / fire / SOS / failed fallback. Immediate escalation, no debounce.
P1ODD exit / MRM / critical fault / unknown active state. Hold capacity, urgent response.
P2Assistance / obstruction / boarding failure. Assess exposure and escalate if worsening.
P3Noncritical service or diagnostic issue. Schedule work under explicit restrictions.

Vehicle I04 / roadside I09 remain separate source envelopes. I09 adds coverageRef, frame/map/calibrationRev, clock bound and source lineage. Preserve original observation time; repeated or replayed samples never refresh it.

Clear only after valid samples span an agreed stable interval. ACK does not clear health. Common-cause grouping retains vehicle exposure and deadlines. Snooze needs reason/expiry and cannot suppress P0. Missing/invalid data raise their own event.

D17.1State machineAlarm lifecycle: validate / detect → correlate / assign → act / verify → clear, with reopen and escalation

The three stages of 10.2 as a lifecycle with its exits. ACK assigns ownership but never clears health; clearing needs a stable clear condition; contradictory evidence reopens. Missing or invalid data leave the main path as their own event. Ownership that lapses is reassigned, not abandoned.

TransitionGuardEffect

6 missing / invalidSample fails identity, schema, unit, epoch/seq, age or clock boundOwn event; remote state UNKNOWN for that signal

P1ODD exit / MRM / critical fault / unknown active stateHold capacity, urgent responseReason + expiry required
P2Assistance / obstruction / boarding failureAssess exposure; escalate if worseningReason + expiry required

Orthogonal states and guarded return to service

RM-05. ADS operation, assistance workflow, remote knowledge and fleet eligibility are separate dimensions. An ADS can continue its approved local behaviour while a remote assistance request is pending.

11.1Vehicle-reported operating state: selected transitions

11.2Assistance lifecycle runs independently of ADS operation

  1. REQUESTED / ASSIGNED
    • SceneRef + requestId + dueAt
    • Qualified owner + bounded lease
  2. ADVICE / VEHICLE REVIEW
    • Current scene / capability / expiry
    • ADS accepts or rejects advice
  3. RESOLVED / ESCALATED
    • Observed outcome or owned follow-up
    • No implied ADS mode transition

Remote knowledge

CURRENT / DEGRADED / UNKNOWN is per required signal. Fresh data may still report a fault. Unknown physical execution blocks conflicting reuse.

Fleet eligibility / case state

AVAILABLE / RESTRICTED / HELD differs from OPEN / ACTIVE / CLOSED. Closing a case never changes ADS mode or automatically clears an operational hold.

D18.1State machineAssistance request lifecycle, independent of ADS mode

The three stages of 11.2 split into their states and exits, following the P19 RM-06A sequence. Every transition changes only the assistance workflow; ADS mode, remote knowledge and fleet eligibility move independently (for example DDT_ACTIVE + RA_PENDING).

VVehicle evidence

  • Current, mutually consistent required signals

  • Cause removed or approved restriction recorded
  • Field / inspection work complete if required

  • Current case revision + valid release authority
  • No blocking incident or unresolved command

FFeasible mission

  • Passenger outcome known; D1 permit current
  • Route, energy and resource bundle reconciled
↓
RELEASE_ELIGIBLE = V ∧ C ∧ A ∧ F
  • Guarded approval allows C03 to reassess availability.
  • It does not command the ADS to move.

Test cross-products, not only one state chain: DDT_ACTIVE + RA_PENDING; MRC + stale evidence; CLOSED case + critical fault; fresh telemetry + unresolved command. A reported zero speed never suffices for MRC or restart.

The four predicates of 11.3 evaluated as a conjunction. Each predicate is checked on its own evidence; a passing predicate never compensates for a failing one. Only a full pass lets C03 reassess availability, and even then no command is sent to the ADS.

Fence contract: vehicle durably stores its accepted authority epoch and validates signed grants, expiry and command identity. Reboot without recoverable authority/journal evidence blocks new action until resynchronised.

Centre ownership loss blocks new dispatch, but cannot erase an already accepted physical effect. No automatic resend with a new ID. An unsupported fence/dedup capability excludes automated centre handover for that vehicle.

D20.3State machinePer-vehicle authority epoch and fence

The fence contract as a per-vehicle state machine, from the vehicle’s point of view. New authority exists only after the vehicle durably stores the epoch and acknowledges it; reconciliation of old effects and the P18 release predicates still gate any new mission.

1 old epoch → UNKNOWNLoss of fresh evidenceHold capacity / preserve incident ownership; no new motion-enabling action

7 rebootReboot without recoverable authority / journal evidenceNew action blocked until resynchronised

Fence validation onboard: signed grants, expiry and command identity. No automatic resend with a new ID.

14.3Workload and scenario acceptance

Staffing input:

A = Σ(λ_k × E[S_k]) in matched time units.

A/m is a mean-load screen, not a service-level guarantee. Test bursts, breaks, common-cause alarms, handover and centre loss. Include field-team travel and replacement-trip capacity separately. Record detection, ACK, resolution, overdue cases and failed recovery. Restrict new commitments when response capacity is exhausted. P27 defines service-mode and return-to-service gates. Every open branch retains an owner and deadline.

15.3Freshness uses bounded clock error and future-time rejection

Δ_i = t_now − t_observed,i     U_i = u_source,i + u_observer
ageUpper_i = max(0, Δ_i + U_i)
timeOK_i = boundsKnown ∧ clocksValid ∧ (Δ_i ≥ −U_i) ∧ (ageUpper_i ≤ F_i)
valid_i = identityOK ∧ schemaOK ∧ sourceOK ∧ epoch/sequenceOK ∧ timeOK_i
  • All terms use seconds. U includes synchronisation error and drift since the last trusted update.
  • No finite clock bound means time validity is UNKNOWN. Local timers use a monotonic clock.

Response and execution deadlines

D_remote = D_detect + D_queue + D_ack + D_assess + D_transmit + D_accept. Budget is operational. Do not use it to justify onboard safety deadlines. Expiry uses the receiver’s validated time bound; clock uncertainty rejects new time-critical acceptance.

Ownership and release parameters

ADS owner: local link-loss/fallback, action capability, fence and journal persistence. Platform: F_i, clock bounds, sampling, loss, retry and retention. Operations: response class, seat/field coverage and escalation. Each value needs a unit, rationale and boundary test.

D22.3Decision logicPer-signal freshness validation and its outcomes

valid_i evaluated as an ordered chain of the terms in 15.3. Each failing term has its own outcome; none of them defaults a missing state to healthy, and none blocks read-only queries or emergency escalation.

Owner of F_i
Platform: F_i, clock bounds, sampling, loss, retry and retention. Each value needs a unit, rationale and boundary test.
Local timers
Use a monotonic clock. Expiry uses the receiver’s validated time bound; clock uncertainty rejects new time-critical acceptance.
Test
Future timestamps, unknown clock bounds and expired authority (T-R01, P24 17.1).

Source: P22 15.3–15.4; P17 10.2; P18; P24 17.1

15.4Audit scope and evidence lifecycle

Purpose-limited capture, scoped access, encryption, retained incident evidence and read-only replay. AI may draft or summarise within task scope; it cannot independently authorise ADS movement. Test cross-tenant access, expired authority, future timestamps, unknown clock bounds and duplicate effects.

Desk-reviewed architecture proposal; implementation, performance and safety validation remain pending. Public references support terminology and patterns, not this system’s certification. Sources in notes: SAE J3016 baseline, ISO 34503, NHTSA, Waymo, NPA, AWS, Microsoft, Hazelcast, PostgreSQL, RFC 5905 and calendar API documentation.

Degraded operation and recovery capacity

Operational continuity requires bounded service reductions, passenger support and a verified return to service. Recovery uses the same finite fleet, site and staffing resources.

20.1Failure propagation across the service system

Demand pressure

  • Peak arrivals / directional imbalance
  • Longer trips / slow turnaround

Supply loss

  • Vehicle fault / site outage / energy shortfall
  • Communication loss / staff absence
↓
↓

Impact assessment

  • Identify affected bookings and intervals. Recompute reachable vehicles, usable hubs and qualified response capacity.
  • Preserve already accepted commitments and unknown physical effects. Record unmet demand and passenger exposure.
↓
  1. NORMAL
    • Service promise feasible
    • Capacity and evidence current
  2. CONSTRAINED
    • Restrict new offers by zone / time
    • Protect accepted journeys
  3. SUSPENDED
    • Stop affected new commitments
    • Maintain support and local fallback

Transitions use configured triggers, persistence and owner approval. Recovery thresholds include hysteresis to avoid repeated entry / exit. Local ADS safety decisions remain independent of this service-mode model.

The three service modes of 20.1 as a state machine. Entry uses a configured trigger, persistence and owner approval; exit uses recovery thresholds with hysteresis to avoid repeated entry / exit, and offers widen only after sustained recovery is observed.

The service mode governs admission of new commitments only. It does not change ADS mode; closing a case never automatically clears an operational hold.

20.2Parallel passenger, asset and capacity recovery

Passenger outcome

  • Contact every affected passenger party
  • Explain revised ETA / alternatives
  • Reserve feasible replacement journeys
  • Track each handover and resolution
  • Own compensation / refund decision

Vehicle / site outcome

  • Retain fault and command history

  • Observe secure state and clearance

  • Reconcile unresolved physical effects

Resource outcome

  • Reserve relief / field capacity
  • Cargo custody / storage / returns
  • Revise passenger / cargo plans
  • Include staff travel and queues
  • Escalate recovery shortfall

20.3Return-to-service gate and staffing condition

Return-to-service gate

  • Cause addressed + fresh evidence + authorised release + feasible next mission + passenger outcome resolved.
  • Connectivity restoration alone cannot release capacity.
  • Observe sustained recovery before widening offers.

Response capacity

A = Σ λ_k E[S_k] in matched time units.
  • A < qualified staffed seats is only a mean-load screen.
  • Test bursts, common-cause alarms, breaks and travel.
  • Every open case needs an owner, deadline and backup.
  • Keep field response separate from remote assistance.

Record trigger, affected scope, admission restriction, accountable owner, next review and recovery evidence for each degraded period.

D27.3Decision logicReturn-to-service gate as a decision flow

The five conjuncts of the gate evaluated in order. Any failed check keeps the capacity held; connectivity restoration alone never passes the gate. The gate corresponds to the release predicate RELEASE_ELIGIBLE = V ∧ C ∧ A ∧ F, after which C03 may reassess availability.

Source: P27 20.3; P18 11.3; P14 7.1

Operating feasibility and verification evidence

A configuration qualifies only within its tested demand, geography and operating conditions. Service quality, resource limits, recovery and economics require separate evidence.

21.1Measurement chain and explicit denominators

  1. RequestsUnique service intents
  2. DispatchVerified assignment
  3. PickupPhysical arrival
  4. CompletionVerified trip outcome

Service quality

  • Dispatch success = assigned / eligible dispatch requests.
  • Keep capacity and admission rejects in the denominator.
  • Demand fulfillment = completed / eligible requests.
  • Report customer cancellations separately by reason.

Pickup and utilization

Wait starts at request time for immediate demand, or agreed pickup time for a reservation. Report p50 / p95 with the observed-arrival count and missing outcomes. Show on-time pickups / pickups due, including failures. Separate available hours from scheduled fleet hours.

At cut-off, classify every passenger booking and shipment separately: completed, cancelled, rejected, expired, unresolved or active. A pooled mission is not one passenger request. Retain people counts separately from booking counts. Show exclusions, censoring and missing evidence.

D28.1Data flowMeasurement chain from intent to verified outcome

Each stage of 21.1 takes its count from the component that owns the evidence. Rejections and cancellations leave the chain as classified outcomes; they are never dropped from the denominator.

Source: P28 21.1; P10 3.1; P08 1.1; P02 02

Each measure of 21.1 with only the numerator, denominator and treatment rules the chapter states. Cells left as “not stated” are not defined in the document.

Counting unit

21.2Reproducible scenario design and pass conditions

  1. Freeze inputs
    • Passenger / cargo OD and windows
    • Lead time and sharing acceptance
    • Party, mass, volume and handling time
    • Fleet, hubs and response limits
    • Input / policy / route revisions
  2. Exercise conditions
    • Single-party / pooling / cargo / both
    • Peak and directional concentration
    • Vehicle / hub / energy capacity loss
    • No-show / failed cargo handover
    • Combined faults and recovery ramp
  3. Evaluate each case
    • Passenger and freight service gates
    • Seats, payload, volume and energy
    • Detour, dwell and recovery workload
    • Unserved / unresolved outcomes
    • Binding constraint and owner

PASS RECORD

State target, denominator, time window and acceptance rule before running. Use repeatable demand traces or recorded seeds, then independent trials. Preserve every run and failure. Finite synthetic tests establish a tested envelope only. Pilot evidence determines field readiness.

21.3Capacity decision and business consequence

Feasible alternatives

Compare fleet, hub placement and service policy only after all required operating conditions pass. Rank cost within the feasible tested set. If none qualifies, report the binding constraint and re-plan.

Economic reconciliation

  • Reconcile passenger fares and freight revenue.
  • Count shared route / infrastructure costs once.
  • Include dwell, displaced trips, handling and returns.
  • Separate operating contribution, CAPEX and cash flow.

Release evidence: input revision, scenario / seed, execution trace, metric definitions, pass / fail by condition, residual restriction and accountable decision. Operational feasibility does not by itself establish project profitability or safety certification.

D28.3State machineScenario and pass-record lifecycle

A run moves from a frozen input set to an accountable decision. The pass record is fixed before running; every run and failure is preserved; a feasible tested set feeds the capacity decision of 21.3, otherwise the binding constraint triggers a re-plan.

Stress cases

Evidence: route revision, ordered stops, segment occupancy, accepted detour / fare, actual passenger times and booking-level outcomes. Show total contribution and passenger fulfillment together. Higher occupancy can coexist with fewer completed journeys. Agree thresholds and operating authority before pilot release.

23.2Capacity is a vector at each route segment

Independent constraints

Passenger seats and accessible positions remain within their configured limits.

Σ_j cargoVolume_j,s ≤ usableCargoVolume_s   and   Σ_j onboardMass_j,s ≤ payloadLimit_s
  • Onboard mass includes people, luggage and cargo under the same payload boundary.
  • Check segregation, securement, door access and passenger comfort before accepting a job.

Time and recovery constraint

  • Route time = travel + passenger dwell + cargo handling + required turnaround.
  • Recompute every pickup, arrival and delivery ETA.
  • Cargo waiting / failed handover consumes capacity.
  • Protect passenger recovery and energy reserve.

Service policy and authority

  • Use an approved vehicle / goods combination.
  • Confirm transport, insurance and partner eligibility.
  • Assign loading, custody and exception owners.
  • Decline cargo that breaks passenger commitments.
  • Apply return / storage rules after failed delivery.
D30.2Data modelCapacity vector at one route segment

Each route segment carries independent capacity dimensions. A job is accepted only when every dimension holds on every segment it occupies; no dimension compensates for another.

Time is checked separately: route time = travel + passenger dwell + cargo handling + required turnaround, and every pickup, arrival and delivery ETA is recomputed.

Source: P30 23.2; P29 22.2

23.3Four operating conditions on the same demand basis

Single-party

No pooling / cargo

Shared rides

Cargo only

Economic comparison

Δ contribution = Δ passenger revenue + freight revenue − Δ total attributable operating cost
  • Passenger revenue reflects discounts and displaced / unserved trips. Do not subtract that loss twice.
  • Include handling, detours, energy, cleaning, support, returns / claims and app cost. Count route cost once.

23.4Outcome and failure evidence

Report passenger fulfillment / delay and freight delivery / lateness separately, plus vehicle-hours, payload / volume limits, dwell and total contribution. Test full payload, long unloading, absent recipient, incompatible goods, cancellation and vehicle loss. Keep passenger and shipment identities within one shared mission. Hold effects 01–03 constant across the four conditions, then test interactions.

D30.3VerificationFour-condition comparison matrix

The four operating conditions of 23.3 run on the same demand basis, fleet, hubs and faults, with effects 01–03 held constant. Each column reports the same outcome set so that Δ contribution = Δ passenger revenue + freight revenue − Δ total attributable operating cost and the service outcomes can be read side by side.

ItemSingle-partyShared ridesPassenger + cargoCombined
PoolingOffOnOffOn
CargoOffOffOnOn
Passenger fulfillment / delayReportedReportedReportedReported
Freight delivery / lateness——ReportedReported
Vehicle-hours, dwellReportedReportedReportedReported

Stress testConstraint pressuredRequired handling
Full payloadpayloadLimit_sDecline cargo that breaks passenger commitments
Long unloadingRoute time, passenger windowsRecompute every pickup, arrival and delivery ETA
Absent recipientCargo waiting consumes capacityFailed-attempt proof; apply return / storage rules
Incompatible goodsApproved vehicle / goods combinationDecline; segregation checked before accepting a job

Cost rule
Passenger revenue reflects discounts and displaced / unserved trips; that loss is not subtracted twice. Route cost is counted once.
Order
Hold effects 01–03 constant across the four conditions, then test interactions.

Owns
D2 route / segment capacity and bundles: ResourceBundle, ResourceInterval (P10 3.1).
Invariants
One D2 transaction per bundle resource set. Atomic guarantees cover D2 only. Exclusive: no overlap; pooled: sum ≤ capacity. Shared seats enforce summed capacity per segment.
Replacement
Replacement holds new capacity before retiring old. Swap applies only to unstarted allocations. Started/unknown missions retain occupancy until physical clearance.
Pending
PENDING does not expire on quote TTL; PENDING occupancy stays blocked during unknown external effects. Unknown ≠ rejection.
States
REQUESTED → HELD / REJECTED; HELD → COMMIT_PENDING / EXPIRED; COMMIT_PENDING → CONFIRMED / RECONCILING; CONFIRMED → IN_SERVICE → COMPLETED (D09.3).

B.VTZFunctional blocksVehicle trust zone

The vehicle trust zone (device identity, boot epoch and capability revision) holds the ADS local safety authority, the edge adapter / durable journal and the media / passenger interface. Level 4 ADS retains DDT and fallback authority; remote monitoring, contextual assistance and passenger support use separate permissions and evidence paths.

BlockFunction (as stated)Inputs → outputsStore / interfaceDetail views
ADS / local safety authorityOEDR: detect and respond to road events. DDT: tactical / operational driving. Perception, localisation, motion control. DDT fallback initiates local response. B.C09Functional blocksC09 Event backbone

C09 is the event backbone: at-least-once delivery + transactional outbox + idempotent inbox + replay isolation. It distributes BookingChanged, AllocationCommitted, MissionObserved, EnergyUpdated, UsageVerified and CaseChanged from each owner's outbox to scoped subscribers.

Durable state holds outbox + command journal.Owner commit → committed event in outboxD1–D7 logical stores (outbox + command journal)D10.1 · D08.1
At-least-once deliveryC09 event delivery from each owner's transactional outbox with per-aggregate revision.Outbox → event envelope to each subscriberBroker / consumers (operations)D08.1 · D08.3
Idempotent inboxInbox deduplication per consumer; a duplicate has no second effect.Envelope (eventId) → new or duplicateIdempotent inbox per consumerD10.3
Revision checkInbox dedup → revision check → apply / fetch gap / quarantine.aggregateId, aggregateRevision → apply, fetch gap or quarantineScoped event subscriptionsD10.3
Replay isolationReplay must use separate projections and idempotent effect handlers; RECONCILE rebuilds projections and verifies external effects by original IDs.Historical events → rebuilt projections without effectSeparate projectionsD08.2 · D24.2
QuarantineEvents that cannot be applied are quarantined; lag + poison-event alerts.Unappliable event → quarantine + alertBroker / consumersD10.3

At-least-once delivery + transactional outbox + idempotent inbox + replay isolation.

BookingChanged / AllocationCommitted / MissionObserved / EnergyUpdated / UsageVerified / CaseChanged.

Scoped event subscriptions cross the trust boundary with authenticated domain commands. Replay must use separate projections and idempotent effect handlers.

OPS-085Each outcome shall be recorded as a CommandAuditEvent carrying RECEIVED / ACCEPTED / REJECTED / EXECUTING / COMPLETED / ABORTED / EXPIRED with a reason, stateRevision, evidenceRefs, policyVersion and actor, together with producerId, bootEpoch, streamId, sequence, observedAt, receivedAt and clock-bound metadata.C04, C06P22 15.2 RM-10I · D22.2
OPS-086Raw events and validation results shall be kept append-only, and UNKNOWN shall be recorded as the observer's knowledge, not as an ADS state.C04, C06P22 15.2 RM-10I · D22.2
OPS-087Remote-operation evidence shall use purpose-limited capture, scoped access, encryption, retained incident evidence and read-only replay.C06, OrgP22 15.4 RM-10I · —
OPS-088Audit and guard testing shall cover cross-tenant access, expired authority, future timestamps, unknown clock bounds and duplicate effects.OrgP22 15.4 RM-10T · D22.3 · T-R01 · T-R04

AI tool pipeline limits

IDRequirementAllocated toSourceVerification
OPS-089Service AI shall not authorise motion; AI may draft or summarise within task scope but shall not independently authorise ADS movement.C06, C08P14 7.1 RM-02 · P22 15.4 RM-10 · P23 16.2T · D23.3 · T-R08
OPS-090An AI proposal shall pass typed schema and consent validation and deterministic constraints, and shall execute only as an idempotent domain command under role, tool allowlist and lease, with independent guards enforcing consent and accepted terms and a trace in D7.C06, C08P23 16.2T · D23.3
OPS-091An AI proposal that is outside scope, low confidence, adds cost or involves a custody exception shall go to a human decision.C06, C08P23 16.2T · D23.3
OPS-092AI automation shall be released in stages (shadow comparison → staff-approved actions → bounded automatic tasks), and model updates shall require offline evaluation and versioned release.C08, OrgP23 16.2I · D23.3

Verification coverage and release dependencies

IDRequirementAllocated toSourceVerification
OPS-093Remote-operation requirements shall join the PaaS acceptance plan, and the fault-injection cases T-R01 to T-R08 shall show their observable invariants before release; release shall require reproducible evidence and operating readiness.OrgP24 17.1 RM-11T · D24.1 · T-R01 · T-R08 · G3
OPS-094Each fault-injection run shall record the scenario / ODD slice, initial state, revisions, injected fault, trace and oracle result, tested in SIL / HIL / operator / vehicle trials as applicable.OrgP24 17.3 RM-11I · D24.1 · G3
OPS-095Verification shall test the orthogonal-state cross-products DDT_ACTIVE + RA_PENDING, MRC + stale evidence, CLOSED case + critical fault and fresh telemetry + unresolved command, not only one state chain.OrgP18 11.3 RM-05 · P24 17.1 RM-11T · D18.3
OPS-096After a fault with an uncertain effect, the platform shall quarantine the affected resource, query the original intent or cmdId and preserve observed / source times, and shall recover from the durable journal by rebuilding projections without effect.C04, C06, C03P24 17.2 RM-11T · D24.2 · T-R04 · T-R06
OPS-097When the deadline is reached with the outcome still unknown, the uncertainty shall be retained as an owned exception with deadline, backup owner and fallback, and re-entry shall be authorised only on current evidence and valid state.C06P24 17.2 RM-11T · D24.2 · T-R07

C.8Roadside sensing requirements (RSD)

Topology, ownership and planes

IDRequirementAllocated toSourceVerification
RSD-001Roadside observations shall supplement vehicle evidence and feed monitoring and operational review only; I09 shall not provide direct actuation.C10, C06P15 8.1 RM-13T · D15.1
RSD-002Roadside sensing, edge compute and communication functions shall have separate ownership.OrgP15 8.1 RM-13I · —
RSD-003Roadside sensing shall deliver on I09a time stamps with calibrationRef, coverage polygon with occlusion, and health / quality / sensor revision, within a field trust zone of site-scoped identity, clock and calibration.OrgP15 8.1 RM-13I · D15.1
RSD-004The edge / MEC observation worker shall transform local frames to the agreed map frame and publish on I09b scoped tracks with quality and lineage, using a bounded buffer and priority queues.OrgP15 8.1 RM-13T · D15.1
RSD-005The RSU and backhaul gateway shall use authenticated IP transport with separate identity, profile and rate limit, and shall not be assumed to integrate sensing.OrgP15 8.1 RM-13I · D15.1
RSD-006Edge management shall run on a separate control plane with signed model and config versions, staged release and rollback, and CPU, memory, queue age and sensor health monitoring.OrgP15 8.1 RM-13I · —
RSD-007Regional failover shall use a new epoch and re-qualify observations.C10P15 8.1 RM-13T · D16.1
RSD-008The PPA site services / installation contract shall cover power capacity, backup autonomy, thermal budget, cabinet, network, physical access and maintenance, with a separate sensor site where coverage requires it.OrgP15 8.1 RM-13I · —

C10 ingestion checks and quarantine

IDRequirementAllocated toSourceVerification
RSD-009C10 shall apply I09c schema / source / access checks to every envelope before C06 receives it.C10P15 8.1 RM-13 · P16 9.1 RM-14T · D15.3 · D16.3
RSD-010C10 shall apply clock bound, age and sequence gates; an envelope with an unknown clock bound shall be rejected with time validity UNKNOWN.C10P15 8.1 RM-13 · P16 9.1 RM-14T · D16.3
RSD-011C10 shall apply frame / calibration / coverage checks.C10P15 8.1 RM-13T · D15.3 · D16.3
RSD-012C10 shall classify each envelope as accepted, quarantine or diagnostic; an invalid, stale, unknown-clock-bound, bad-calibration or lost-coverage envelope shall be quarantined, not silently dropped, and the source shall receive a reject / diagnostic receipt.C10P15 8.3 RM-13 · P16 9.1 RM-14T · D15.3 · D16.3
RSD-013A coverage failure shall publish coverage degradation with an owner to C06.C10, C06P15 8.3 RM-13 · P16 9.1 RM-14T · D15.3 · D16.3
RSD-014C10 shall deduplicate by source, epoch and sequence, and repeated or replayed samples shall never refresh the original observation time.C10P16 9.1 RM-14 · P17 10.2 RM-03T · D16.1
RSD-015Unknown or lost coverage shall never be interpreted as a clear road.C10, C06P15 8.1 RM-13T · D15.3

ObservationEnvelope and CoverageHealth

IDRequirementAllocated toSourceVerification
RSD-016Each I09c ObservationEnvelope shall carry tenantId, siteId, sourceId, sensorIds[], bootEpoch, seq, observedAt, emittedAt, clockErrorBound_s, expiresAt, trackKey, frameId, mapRev, calibrationRev, coverageRef, position_m, velocity_mps, uncertainty / covariance, class + confidence, visibility, modelRev, evidenceRef and payloadHash, with signature or authenticated transport.C10P15 8.2 RM-13I · D15.2
RSD-017trackKey shall be sourceId / bootEpoch / localTrackId, and no global identity shall be assumed from local track IDs.C10, C06P15 8.2 RM-13T · D15.2
RSD-018CoverageHealth shall report coverageId / polygon / exclusions / sampledAt, sensor availability, clock validity, calibration status and occlusion / weather / queueAge / processing status.C10P15 8.2 RM-13I · D15.2
RSD-019Thresholds for age, association, coverage and queue size shall be agreed per use case and shall not be fixed in this baseline.OrgP15 8.3 RM-13I · G2

Association and correlation in C06

IDRequirementAllocated toSourceVerification
RSD-020C06 shall associate accepted roadside observations with I04 vehicle pose, status, time and quality through a spatial-temporal gate that preserves uncertainty; association shall remain probabilistic.C06P15 8.3 RM-13 · P16 9.1 RM-14T · D16.2
RSD-021Each candidate vehicle link shall carry confidence, method and expiry.C06P15 8.2 RM-13I · D15.2
RSD-022When roadside and vehicle evidence disagree, C06 shall keep both source claims as separate hypotheses and shall not silently override ADS state.C06P15 8.1 RM-13 · P16 9.2 RM-14T · D16.2
RSD-023Multiple reports shall retain source lineage to avoid double counting.C06P15 8.2 RM-13T · D16.2
RSD-024Evidence presented to the operator shall carry quality, provenance and coverage state.C06P15 8.3 RM-13 · P16 9.1 RM-14I · D16.2

Link loss, overload and replay

IDRequirementAllocated toSourceVerification
RSD-025Heartbeat expiry shall set coverage UNKNOWN, retain the source time of the last valid sample and publish coverage degraded with an owner; no stale frame shall be displayed as current.C10, C06P16 9.2 RM-14T · D16.1
RSD-026A reconnecting edge shall use a new epoch and pass resync and health checks before its observations are eligible; replay shall be historical only and shall not act live.C10P15 8.3 RM-13 · P16 9.2 RM-14T · D16.1
RSD-027Under overload the edge shall reserve queue capacity for health / critical events, apply an explicit drop policy and report queue age and dropped observations, and C10 shall quarantine and publish coverage degradation.Org, C10P15 8.3 RM-13 · P16 9.2 RM-14T · D16.2
RSD-028Return of roadside coverage shall never release vehicle capacity; release shall remain with the P18 predicates.C06, C03P16 9.2 RM-14T · D16.1

Evidence handling and guarded response

IDRequirementAllocated toSourceVerification

RSD-030Raw clips shall be governed by a purpose, access and retention contract; edge summaries shall be sent first and authorised evidence on request, returned as EvidenceRef with source / retention.C06, OrgP15 8.3 RM-13 · P16 9.1 RM-14I · —

← BArchitecture viewsD →Interface control and data dictionary

Autonomous mobility service / System planning — Initial conceptAppendix D

Interface control and data dictionary

Provider, consumer, messages, fields, ordering, validity, authority and failure behaviour of each interface, and every named field with its entity and owner. Values the design basis leaves to a later gate are shown as such.

D.1Interface control

One panel per interface I01–I09c and the C09 event backbone. Values restate the document; “—” marks a property the document does not state. Protocols are a G2 decision (P08 1.2).

InterfaceI01 Channel intake (municipal / partner channels → C01)
Provider
C01 API gateway + adapters [application]
Consumer
Municipal / partner channels: resident app / phone / corporate fleet; Outlook, Google, Tabelog, Ikyu, Hot Pepper. C01 passes I01 / confirmed fields to the C02 coordinator, which normalises intent.
Transport
HTTPS (P08 1.1)
Operations / messages
Share plan / time and preferences with consent; need / consent; I01 / confirmed fields → normalise intent (source + conditionsRev). Calendar changes produce proposed intent, never auto-booking by default.
Request fields
PlanReference: tenantId, planRefId, provider, accountRef, sourceEventId, instanceId, sourceRevision, consentId, purpose, expiresAt, startUTC, endUTC, IANA zone.
Result / outcomes
Normalised intent at C02; PlanReference 0..1 : N Booking (FK planRefId optional for app input).
Idempotency and ordering
Unique within tenant: provider / account / event / instance. Source cursor at C01. Capture intent, needs, consent and idempotent request (MVP).
Validity and time
Consent purpose, expiry and withdrawal remain explicit; consent expiresAt; startUTC, endUTC with IANA zone.
Security and authority
Identity, object / tenant access, consent, schema and source cursor at C01. Trust boundary: authenticated domain commands / scoped event subscriptions. Keys include tenant scope.
Failure behaviour
Connector failure may leave local intake available; confirmation still requires all mandatory dependencies. Sync deletion / resync must not erase D1 bookings.
Owner store
PlanReference / C01 (no D-store stated); resulting bookings in D1 (C02).

InterfaceI02 Booking commit / amend / cancel (consoles → C01 → C02)
Provider
C02 Booking / activities (via C01)
Consumer
Operator / provider consoles (transport / activities / parking lessors); client / rider messages to C02 in P11 4.1.
Transport
HTTPS (P08 1.1)
Operations / messages
Commit / amend / cancel. P11 4.1: 01 Quote/amend(reqId); 09 Offer + hold expiry; 10 Terms + expiresAt; 11 Accept(termsRev); 21 Outcome(intent); 22 Cancel(intent,rev); 24 Persisted result; 25 Customer outcome; 26 Permit / keep blocked.
Request fields
reqId; termsRev; intent, rev. Booking: tenantId, bookingId, planRefId, bookingRev, termsRev, state, riderRef, pickupWindow, destination, currentBundleId, intentId.
Result / outcomes
Booking states DRAFT → QUOTED (expiresAt) → PENDING (hold) → CONFIRMED (commit) → IN_SERVICE → COMPLETED / CANCELLED (reason + release); timeout / lost acknowledgement → UNKNOWN. Only CONFIRMED + no pending cancel can issue a current dispatch permit.
Idempotency and ordering
Single writer + transactional outbox. CAS: expectedBookingRev; D1 finalise by CAS. D1 owns bookingRev. Cancel and permit issuance serialize in D1. Never duplicate a side effect.
Validity and time
Quote expiresAt; guard: expired / changed input rejects. Revision conflict → refresh terms; stale evidence → block offer or action with reason.
Security and authority
C01 identity, object / tenant access, consent and schema checks; trust boundary: authenticated domain commands.
Failure behaviour
Interrupt at any phase: D1 records cancelRequested against intent. Cancellation after permit issuance becomes cancel / replan of an in-flight mission, not a guarantee of zero movement. Unknown → query and reconcile.
Owner store
D1 (C02): bookingRev, terms, intent, saga; dispatch permit.

InterfaceI03 Joint reservation (C02 → C03)
Provider
C03 Joint reservation authority
Consumer
C02 Booking / activities (coordinator)
Transport
Not stated (G2 decision: protocols, P08 1.2)
Operations / messages
Quote / hold / atomic replacement; I03 CommitBundle / command. P11 4.1: 02 Plan(terms,windows); 07 Hold(snapshot) → 08 holdId / expiresAt; 13 PromoteHold(intent) → 14 PENDING / reject; 18 CommitSwap(intent) → 19 Durable outcome; 20 Release old / undo new as required.
Request fields
CommitBundle: tenantId, intentId, bookingId, expectedBookingRev, newBundleId, oldBundleId, expectedResourceRevs, acceptedTermsRev, capabilityRev, idempotencyKey.
Result / outcomes
intentId, state (COMMITTED), bundleId, bundleRev, intentIdForD1, committedAt, externalReleaseJobs. Other explicit outcomes HELD / REJECTED / PENDING with reasonCode + retryability. Infeasible: binding reason (+ alternative).
Idempotency and ordering
Same key + different payload: reject IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT. Unique: tenant / intent / key. expectedResourceRevs maps to the ordered resource set; resource revision set + ordered locks; one D2 transaction per bundle resource set; D2 local commit + outbox atomically.
Validity and time
HELD bundle expires (expiresAt); expiry releases unused hold. PENDING does not expire on quote TTL. Policy version + snapshot time; resource snapshot and energy capability are versioned inputs, not one shared revision.
Security and authority
Keys / FKs include tenant scope; validate references within that scope. Ranking never relaxes a hard constraint.
Failure behaviour
Unknown ≠ rejection. Outcome unknown → RECONCILING (query original intent). Replacement holds new capacity before retiring old; swap applies only to unstarted allocations; started / unknown missions retain occupancy until physical clearance. Atomic guarantees cover D2 only.
Owner store
D2 (C03): route / segment capacity and bundles.

InterfaceI04 Mission / receipt / execution (C03 → C04 ↔ vehicle edge)
Provider
C04 Fleet / vehicle adapter
Consumer
Vehicle / AD (vehicle trust zone edge adapter); C06 and C10 consume I04 pose / status / time / quality as evidence.
Transport
Not stated (G2 decision: protocols, P08 1.2). Channels: telemetry / alarm; command / result; evidence / media (P14 7.1).
Operations / messages
Mission / receipt / execution. P13 6.1: 01 Mission(id,validTo); 02 Persist / send cmd; 03 Receipt(cmdId); 04 Accept / reject; 07 Query(cmdId); 08 Execution + seq. P20 13.1: 01 Status(boot,seq); 11 InstallFence(epoch, signed grant); 12 PersistedFenceACK(epoch); 15 Scoped cancel/query under new epoch; 21 New mission(id,epoch,expiry).
Request fields
Mission / Command: tenantId, commandId, bundleId, vehicleId, missionRev, routeRef, validUntil, payloadHash. RemoteActionRequest fields (P22 15.2).
Result / outcomes
Delivery: PERSISTED → SENT → RECEIVED. Execution: ACCEPTED → EXECUTING → COMPLETED / ABORTED. deliveryState, executionState, statusSeq, observedAt, receivedAt. CommandAuditEvent: RECEIVED / ACCEPTED / REJECTED / EXECUTING / COMPLETED / ABORTED / EXPIRED + reason.
Idempotency and ordering
Same commandId: one immutable payloadHash; same ID with changed payload is rejected. Command identity, expiry and dedup at the edge adapter. Query original IDs after lost responses; no automatic resend with a new ID. Verify observedAt / seq / clock quality; old or repeated state cannot prove recovery.
Validity and time
validUntil / validTo. Expiry blocks a new command but never stops status reconciliation. Freshness per P22 15.3 (F_i set by Platform).
Security and authority
C04 obtains the current D1 permit before releasing a mission. Device identity, boot epoch and capability revision; authority fence (vehicle durably stores accepted authority epoch, validates signed grants, expiry and command identity). No cloud override of ADS constraints.
Failure behaviour
Acceptance unknown / fault / stale telemetry → UNKNOWN; block reuse; query; OpenCase. Never default missing state to healthy. Link loss marks remote state UNKNOWN. No fence ACK means no new action. Reboot without recoverable authority / journal evidence blocks new action until resynchronised.
Owner store
D3 (C04): command and status journal.

Not stated (G2 decision: protocols, P08 1.2). External adapters keep a protocol + retry journal (P08 1.2).

Capacity, setpoints, derating; plan journal and execution guard. P11 4.1: 04 Read capability(site,window,minEnergy) → 06 Limits / capabilityRev / age; 15 ReserveEnergy(planId,rev,key) → 16 Accept / reject / unknown; 17 Query same planId until resolved or escalated. Feedback: observed power / energy / meter quality / site alarms (dashed route).
Request fields
planId / planRev / bundleId / capabilityRev / validUntil / powerIntervals[]. EnergyPlan: tenantId, siteId, departureMinKWh, expiresAt, acceptedRev, executionEvidence.
Result / outcomes
ACK / reject / unknown. Plan revision ACK ≠ delivered energy.
Idempotency and ordering
ReserveEnergy carries key; query the same planId. EnergyPlan PK tenantId, planId, planRev. Validate current limits → persist command → send → ACK / reject / unknown.
Validity and time
validUntil; expiresAt; capabilityRev + observedAt + quality; EMS capabilityRev + freshness.
Security and authority
Plant protection remains local; local protection and outage behaviour at site. Market access: eligibility and access gates.
Failure behaviour
Unknown → query status. Rejected / conflict starts compensation; unknown stays blocked. Infeasible → replan (C03). Stale capability or meter data → hold affected assignments. Electrical scope; fuel / H2 requires a separate capability.

InterfaceI07 Case resolution and guarded advice / request (C06 / C08)
Provider
C06 + C08 Operations (cases / policy)
Consumer
Remote operator / RA operator; C04 (guarded advice / request to the vehicle)
Transport
Not stated (G2 decision: protocols, P08 1.2)
Operations / messages
P13 6.1: 10 OpenCase(command, last observation, severity, deadline); 11 Assign(lease,dueAt); 12 ACK(caseRev); 13 Escalate / new lease; 14 Action + evidence; 15 Authorise scoped action; 24 Release decision. P19: 10 Advice(type,scope); 11 GuardedAdvice(ref). P16 9.1: 14 I07 guarded advice / request.
Request fields
RemoteActionRequest: caseId?, expectedCaseRev?, actionType (CONTEXT_ADVICE / STOP_REQUEST / MISSION_CHANGE_REQUEST / STATUS_QUERY), parameters, operatorId, qualificationRef, authorityEpoch, issuedAt, expiresAt, reasonCode, evidenceRefs[], approvalRef?. Action record: vehicle + mission + case revision + lease epoch + reason + advice type + expiry + expected outcome.
Result / outcomes
Case: OPEN → ASSIGNED → ACK → ACTIVE → RESOLVED → CLOSED; material new evidence reopens the case. Receive / accept / reject + reason.
Idempotency and ordering
caseRev guard; command identity per P22 15.2 (same ID with changed payload is rejected).
Validity and time
Lease, dueAt, expiry. Motion-enabling advice requires current contextual evidence; read-only queries and emergency escalation remain available with stale data.
Security and authority
I07 permissions differ by case type. Guard for motion-enabling action: role, caseRev, authority fence, current evidence and expected state. Qualified seat + single action lease. No AI bypass of command guards; AI cannot independently authorise ADS movement. Passenger support cannot override door interlocks or authorise motion.
Failure behaviour
Lease expired / missing ACK / urgent deadline → reject stale action and assign backup owner. Rejected / unknown → keep case open and query state or initiate an approved fallback. Closing a case never changes ADS mode or automatically clears an operational hold.
Owner store
D5 (C06): vehicle cases / owner leases; D7 (C06 + C08): service cases / AI tool traces.

InterfaceI09c Authenticated observations + health (RSU / backhaul → C10 → C06)
Provider
RSU + backhaul gateway (authenticated observations + health)

C10 Roadside ingestion [proposed]; accepted evidence to C06 monitoring + case evidence
Transport
Backhaul: authenticated IP transport; signature / authenticated transport + payloadHash.
Operations / messages
03 Authenticated envelope; 04 Identity / age / frame / dedup; 05 Reject / diagnostic receipt; 06 Coverage degraded + owner; 10 Request scoped clip / history; 12 EvidenceRef + source / retention.
Request fields
ObservationEnvelope: tenantId, siteId, sourceId, sensorIds[], bootEpoch, seq, observedAt, emittedAt, clockErrorBound_s, expiresAt, trackKey, frameId, mapRev, calibrationRev, coverageRef, position_m, velocity_mps, uncertainty / covariance, class + confidence, visibility, modelRev, evidenceRef, payloadHash. CoverageHealth: coverageId / polygon / exclusions / sampledAt, queueAge.
Result / outcomes
Accepted / quarantine / diagnostic. Vehicle association: spatial-temporal gate + uncertainty; candidate link has confidence, method and expiry.
Idempotency and ordering
bootEpoch + seq; dedup at C10. trackKey = sourceId / bootEpoch / localTrackId; no global identity assumed from local track IDs. Multiple reports retain source lineage to avoid double count.
Validity and time
Clock bound + age + sequence gates. Unknown clock bound rejects. Preserve original observation time; repeated or replayed samples never refresh it. Thresholds for age, association, coverage and queue size are agreed per use case.
Security and authority
I09c schema / source / access checks. Feeds monitoring and operational review, not direct actuation; no observation-to-command bypass; advice follows guarded I07 path. Raw clips by purpose + access + retention contract.
Failure behaviour
Invalid / stale / overloaded → quarantine observations, publish coverage degradation. Reserve queue capacity for health / critical events. Drop policy is explicit; historical replay cannot act live. Unknown ≠ clear road. Keep both source claims; no silent override of ADS state.

— (no D-store stated; raw clips under a retention contract)

Inbox dedup → revision check → apply / fetch gap / quarantine.

At-least-once delivery + transactional outbox + idempotent inbox; per-aggregate revision; inbox deduplication.

Outbox in each owning store (D1–D7 logical stores; outbox + command journal in durable state).

E.2Assumptions and constraints

IDAssumption or constraintSource
ASM-001Proposed concept; field validation and implementation pending.P02 · P07
ASM-002Separately prepared models, not copied from Honda internal documents.P01
ASM-003Desk review is complete; implementation and validation remain pending. Diagrams define candidate boundaries and contracts.P08
ASM-004Desk-reviewed architecture proposal; implementation, performance and safety validation remain pending. Public references support terminology and patterns, not this system’s certification.P22 15.4
ASM-005Examples are conceptual payloads, not complete API schemas.P10 3.2
ASM-006The primary service integrates booking, dispatch and energy; equipment / JV / eVTOL options attach through capability interfaces.P08 1.2
ASM-007Atomic guarantees cover D2 only; no distributed atomic commit is assumed. External EMS effects use a reconciled saga.P10 3.2 · P11
ASM-008Provider and transport reservations are not one distributed transaction.P23 16.1
ASM-009Keys / FKs include tenant scope; references are validated within that scope.P10 3.2
ASM-010Level 4 ADS retains DDT and fallback authority. Vehicle / ADS owns driving and fallback.P14 · P13
ASM-011Real-time remote DDT is outside this baseline; no remote steering / throttle baseline.P14 7.2 · P22 15.1
ASM-012RA supplies contextual advice that the ADS can reject after re-evaluating the scene and ODD.P14 7.2
ASM-013Vehicle-specific link-loss and fallback behaviour remains local and does not depend on a remote reply.P14 7.2
ASM-014Local ADS safety decisions remain independent of the service-mode model.P27 20.1
ASM-015AI may draft or summarise within task scope; it cannot independently authorise ADS movement. No AI bypass of command guards.P22 15.4 · P08 1.1
ASM-016Plant protection remains local.P08 1.1
ASM-017I05 has electrical scope; fuel / H2 requires a separate capability.P12 5.1
ASM-018All P are net kW at one AC boundary; conversion losses belong in storage-energy updates, not twice. Electrical: kW, hours, kWh; fuel: kg, kg/min, minutes.P12 5.1 · P26 19.2
ASM-019Availability kW and delivered kWh remain distinct; an energy-plan ACK does not prove delivered energy.P12 · P26 19.2
ASM-020Proposed I09 feeds monitoring and operational review, not direct actuation. The monitoring path does not claim collision avoidance or perception completeness.P15
ASM-021No assumption of integrated sensing; no global identity assumed from local track IDs.P15 8.1–8.2
ASM-022Alarm priorities are operational response classes, not ASIL classifications.P17
ASM-023UNKNOWN is a knowledge state, not a vehicle state; it belongs to the observer, not the ADS.P13 · P22 15.2
ASM-024D_remote is an operational budget; it is not used to justify onboard safety persistence.P22 15.3
ASM-025A/m is a mean-load screen, not a service-level guarantee.P21 14.3 · P27 20.3
ASM-026Calendar changes produce proposed intent, never auto-booking by default. No forced consent or automatic schedule change.P23 · P04
ASM-027Gates are evidence checkpoints, not fixed calendar phases; schedule alone never passes a gate.P07
ASM-028Service feasibility and customer choice remain binding even when aggregate contribution improves.P07
ASM-029Simulation outputs do not establish field impact or guarantee service-level attainment; tests are proposed only.P06
ASM-030The P24 cases are planned tests, not passed results.P24
ASM-031Finite synthetic tests establish a tested envelope only; pilot evidence determines field readiness. A configuration qualifies only within its tested demand, geography and operating conditions.P28
ASM-032Operational feasibility does not by itself establish project profitability or safety certification.P28 21.3
ASM-033Regional workers scale independently of ADS control.P15 8.3
ASM-034Terminology baseline: SAE J3016_202609 (ODD, DDT, OEDR, DDT fallback).P03 MVP control
